look_here_first: Look at narrow rigid rosette leaves, their spaced marginal teeth, and the terminal spine; then inspect the largely spike-like flowering axis. Distinguish A. univittata with leaf-edge detail, not size alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf teeth about 2–6 mm, mostly spaced 2–4 cm apart; terminal spine 1.5–4.5 cm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flowering axis largely spike-like, about 2–3.5 m in the existing FNA-based review.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Rigid narrow leaves in a basal rosette; inspect edge teeth and terminal spine with scale.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Tall largely spicate flowering axis; habit and axis are visible in the USDA photograph, but individual flowers are not resolved.

key_traits.label: Lookalike separators
key_traits.text: A. americana has much broader leaves and a branched panicle. A. univittata has undulate/crenate, less detachable leaf margins and teeth mostly 1–2 cm apart; overlaps require close leaf-edge and flowering evidence. Hybridization is documented in FNA; avoid size-only identification.
